correctness.rationale: For nonnegative length weights w_j, lambda>=0 (not all zero) and n>=3, subset lower-support bounds z(S)=sum of weights of simplices contained in S are *complete*: decompose any test functional into nested suffix indicators and apply separation. A proper subset decomposes into maximal cyclic runs; its centered lower gap A(S) is sum f(run length), f(t)=t(W+lambda/n)−sum_{j<=t}(t−j+1)w_j. Since f(t+1)−f(t)=sum_{j>=t+2}w_j+lambda/n>=0, complementary runs bound A(S)/A(S^c) <= f(n−1)/f(1), equality at a co-singleton. Cyclic averaging proves optimality of the invariant center c=(W+lambda/n)1; saturation of all co-singletons forces uniqueness. Algebra gives the displayed ratio and m-graph filtration values including singleton translation, and symmetry exactly when only w2 remains. Exact rational finite subset enumeration n=3..8 corroborated, not proved general case.
residual_risks: Weights are length-homogeneous nonnegative; arbitrary non-cyclic or signed simplex coefficients excluded.
Constructions use intrinsic affine hyperplane; singleton simplices change center by translation, not asymmetry.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General generalized permutohedron inequalities give a representation framework but do not immediately force the co-singleton extremizer across all nonnegative cyclic interval weights; the monotone run lemma is the new needed step. Other Resultary Minkowski asymmetry formulas apply to stellohedra, matroid bases or cut polytopes, not this cyclic simplex family.

value.rationale: An affine-invariant closed-form asymmetry and unique center for an all-dimensional weighted family of cyclic graph-associahedral simplex sums is an independently useful exact invariant. It quantifies every stage of the natural m-graph polytope filtration and the anomalously smaller last-step increment, beyond known combinatorial and deformation descriptions.
residual_risks: No claim about arbitrary graph-associahedra, arbitrary per-tube weights or Euclidean radii.
